channel.title: The Fimbl blog
channel.description: Guides to calorie tracking apps, mindful eating and habits that last, from the team behind Fimbl, the calm food diary for iPhone and iPad.

item.title: The best progress photo apps in 2026, compared
item.description: Fimbl, Progress, Hevy, MacroFactor, MyFitnessPal and Cronometer compared for progress photos: guided poses, overlays, compare, time-lapse and privacy.

item.title: How accurate is AI calorie tracking, and does it matter?
item.description: AI photo calorie estimates are off by about a third on average, much like manual logging. What studies show, when to trust AI and when to scan a barcode.

item.title: How to track what you eat without counting calories
item.description: Five ways to track food without counting calories: the plate method, hand portions, a hunger scale, a photo food diary and meal grades instead of numbers.

item.title: How to start a food diary: a 7-day plan for beginners
item.description: How to start a food diary that lasts: what to write down, a 7-day beginner plan with one small step a day, and five mistakes that end food diaries early.

item.title: The best calorie tracker apps in 2026, compared side by side
item.description: Fimbl, MyFitnessPal, Cronometer, MacroFactor, Lose It!, YAZIO, Lifesum and Cal AI side by side: what's free, ads, AI logging and who each app suits.

item.title: Why we built a calorie tracker that doesn't judge you
item.description: Why counting alone fails, the six decisions that shaped Fimbl, what we left out on purpose, and our end goal: showing you your own eating patterns.

item.title: Emotional hunger vs physical hunger: how to tell the difference
item.description: How to tell emotional hunger from physical hunger: 7 key differences, a 1–10 hunger scale and a 10-second check-in for when a craving isn't about food.
